title: OpenBaoTransitClient: validate subjectId before path interpolation (path-injection)
description:
HIGH security finding (automated security review of PR #34). engine/src/Babelstone.Pii/OpenBaoTransitClient.cs interpolates subjectId into the OpenBao transit request path unvalidated:

  KeyName(subjectId) => $"pii-{subjectId}"
  used in v1/{mount}/encrypt|decrypt/{KeyName}, v1/{mount}/keys/{KeyName}[/config]

A subjectId containing '/', '..', or URL-special chars could inject a path segment or escape the key namespace (path traversal / URL injection / SSRF-shaped). 'Internal-only' is not a valid dismissal — internal services are common targets, and subjectId may originate from upstream data.

Transit key names are limited to [a-zA-Z0-9_-] anyway (the code comments this charset but does not enforce it). Fix: validate subjectId against [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ in KeyName and throw ArgumentException on violation (reject, do not silently mangle), so every call path (encrypt/decrypt/destroy/ensure-key/key-exists) is guarded at the single chokepoint. Add a Docker-free unit test asserting malicious ids ('../../sys/health', slashes, spaces, query chars, empty) are rejected.

Relates to ADR-PC-004 (PII crypto seam). Shipped in A.5 (archie-qzlb).
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #35 (da3d5a3). subjectId validated at the KeyName chokepoint; path-injection closed.

title: ADR-PC-010: Engine implementation language and process model
description:
The integration-concept ADRs pick infrastructure (broker, registry, gateway) but deliberately do not pick a language for the engine itself. The engine has its own constraints that may force the choice in a different direction from any individual integration component.

Candidates: C# (on .NET), Elixir, Go, Rust, TypeScript on Node. JVM languages (Java, Kotlin, Scala) are explicitly out of scope; C# is in scope because the CLR is a separate runtime family.

Decision criteria:
- LLM-codability (engine-specific). The engine will be authored primarily by an LLM, so the language must offer (a) deep representation in current training corpora, (b) a strong compile-time or type guardrail that catches plausible LLM mistakes before runtime, (c) convention-heavy idioms over expressive metaprogramming the model has to reason about, and (d) lint/format/test tooling tight enough to serve as an outer iteration loop. Languages with known LLM friction — Rust's borrow checker, Elixir's thinner corpus — must be evaluated against this drag.
- Event-store client maturity for the choice landing in ADR-PC-001.
- Typed-schema tooling fit for the choice landing in ADR-PC-006 (CUE, Pkl, etc. have varying language bindings).
- Numerical correctness for EUR retail banking math (decimal arithmetic — feature-design-event-store-projections handler discipline; financial_concepts cash-flow primitive). C# is the only candidate that ships a native 128-bit decimal as a built-in type (`System.Decimal`); the others rely on libraries (Go's shopspring/decimal, Rust's rust_decimal, TS's big.js / decimal.js, Elixir's Decimal). For the non-C# candidates, library ergonomics and protection against accidental float coercion are what differentiate them.
- Operability by a 1–2 person team (ADR-IC-000 S1) and ecosystem coherence with the ADR-IC-* stack (S2).
- Single-codebase commitment (00-product-vision §5).
- Portuguese-market context. EUR-only math (folds into numerical correctness above); a thin local talent pool for human hand-off / incident response — the LLM-coding assumption reduces but does not eliminate the cost of picking an exotic language relative to the Lisbon developer ecosystem.

Process model: single deployable vs modular monolith vs micro-modules. The brief commits to 'one codebase, one set of images' (00-product-vision §5); the within-process module boundaries remain open.

Source: implicit gap — the brief commits to a build but does not pick a language.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-010 (C# .NET 9 + hand-rolled event-sourcing core). Re-decided 2026-05-23: dropped Marten + Wolverine as runtime dependencies (libraries that manage their own tables) in favour of a hand-rolled thin module on PostgreSQL implementing the ADR-PC-001 P1-P5 contract, the ADR-IC-004 outbox, and the ADR-IC-003 in-house orchestrator directly. No IC-003 amendment needed (reverted). Marten/Wolverine kept as working reference implementations. Collateral: ADR-PC-001 amendment (library deferral filled with hand-rolled module). See docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/ADR-PC-010-dotnet-hand-rolled-engine.md.

title: ADR-PC-009: Per-instance pack and schema version pinning
description:
Two stability invariants run in parallel per 01-product-architecture §5: every constituted instance pins to the pack version AND the family-schema version active at constitution, and carries both for its entire life.

Decide:
1. Storage shape of the pinning fact (columns on the instance projection? Envelope fields on every event? Separate registry?).
2. Replay-time lookup: how a handler running at time T0 resolves the pack vN.M and schema vN.M active for instance I.
3. PackVersionMigrated and SchemaVersionMigrated event semantics — payload, when emitted, how downstream projections react (per 02-v1-scope-term-deposits §2.4.2).
4. Q-N: breaking-change opt-in mechanics — explicit POST /v1/pack-adoptions, no silent upgrades.
5. Pack-effective-date placeholder for §8 (per-primitive pin-or-float policy, v2-relevant).

Coordinates with ADR-PC-007 (pack manifest) and ADR-PC-006 (schema language).

Source: 01-product-architecture §5, feature-design-configuration-surface §3.5-§3.6, feature-design-configuration-authoring §6.
close_reason: ADR-PC-009 drafted (Status: Proposed): pack/schema versions pinned on the event envelope (per-event, not per-instance) and resolved via pack_versions/schema_versions registries; projection-only and separate-registry candidates rejected on replay-correctness (cannot represent the migration boundary, circular/dual-write); PackVersionMigrated/SchemaVersionMigrated operator-initiated one-per-instance; Q-N opt-in via POST /v1/pack-adoptions (adoption != migration); pack-effective-date a reserved v1 no-op. title: ADR-PC-008: Rate-sheet storage and deploy API

Decide:
1. Storage shape (table-per-rate-sheet, time-series store, KV with version stamping).
2. Deploy API (POST /v1/rate-sheets style with idempotency keys, separate from product-config deploy path).
3. Version resolution at constitution (rate_sheet_version_id on DepositConstituted per 02-v1-scope-term-deposits §2.4.1; how the engine resolves 'the rate sheet effective on this date for this product variant').
4. Approval / sign-off workflow integration (treasury / ALM ownership per 01-product-architecture §3 table).
5. Q-J typo-rollback mechanics (forward-only fix plus out-of-band compensation — confirm structural support).

Source: feature-design-configuration-surface §2.2, 01-product-architecture §3.

title: ADR-PC-006: Family-schema language and validator runtime
description:
Pick the schema language for typed family schemas with variants, evolving under coarse-start fine-drift (the resolved configuration model — Open Question 4 in 04-open-questions.md, full treatment in feature-design-configuration-authoring §9). The schema is the boundary; no DSL escape hatch.

Candidates: JSON Schema, CUE, Pkl, Avro-as-config, hand-rolled typed DSL.

Decision criteria:
- Supports union types, optional fields, range-bounded scalars, pack-bound primitives (per the §9 four-outcome operational procedure: variant reshape / schema fine-drift / primitive release / roadmap-layer decline).
- Validator runtime supports the 6-depth validator surface from feature-design-configuration-surface §3.6.
- Schema-evolution semantics for fine-drift split-merge (interacts with Q-V; the chosen language must support the split-merge tooling story even if Q-V remains open).
- IDE / authoring ergonomics (relevant to Q-T raw-YAML vs form-UI question, but not gated by it).
- Falsifiability preservation: a variant that 'needs' engine code reveals a schema gap or a primitive gap, never a language bypass (per feature-design-configuration-authoring §7.1).

Coordinates with ADR-PC-007 (pack manifest): pack primitives are typed inside family schemas; schema language and pack format should compose cleanly.

Source: 04-open-questions.md §4 (resolved); feature-design-configuration-authoring §6, §9; feature-design-configuration-surface §3.6.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-006 (CUE + purpose-built Go validator). Re-decided 2026-05-23: dropped the prior JSON Schema + NJsonSchema pick in favour of CUE for native cross-field expressiveness at depths 3-4; validator is a single static Go binary embedding cuelang.org/go, invoked out-of-process; JSON Schema retained as named fallback. title: ADR-PC-005: DR / RTO / RPO posture for the event store
description:
Production-blocking for v1 cutover. The event store is the engine's source of truth; an event-store-volume loss is unrecoverable from projections alone.

Decide:
1. Backup cadence (continuous WAL shipping, hourly snapshots, daily snapshots).
2. Off-site replication topology (warm standby, cold standby, multi-region).
3. RTO / RPO targets (named numbers, not vague 'fast' / 'small').
4. Cold-replay budget under a *recovery* scenario — distinct from the Q-Z benchmark which measures normal-operations cold replay.

Coordinates with ADR-PC-001 (event store tech — different stores have different replication primitives) and ADR-PC-003 (snapshot infrastructure — snapshots accelerate recovery).

Source: Q-AT in 04-open-questions.md.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-PC-005 (DR/RTO/RPO). WAL streaming + synchronous off-site warm standby + PITR; RPO≈0 for committed events, named RTO/RPO numbers (POC defaults pending bank sign-off); projections/snapshots recovered by rebuild; OpenBao key-store DR coordinated; multi-region deferred. Corrected source citation to Q-AY (issue said Q-AT). Production-blocking. See docs/product-management/product_concepts/adrs/ADR-PC-005-dr-rto-rpo.md.

title: ADR-PC-004: PII encryption envelope and key management (crypto-shredding)
description:
Implement §7 of 04-open-questions.md's position: PII fields encrypted per data subject under a per-subject key; erasure = key destruction; cipher-text remains in the event log, plaintext unrecoverable.

Decide:
1. KMS / key-store choice (HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, GCP KMS, pgcrypto, custom HSM-backed). Must be self-hostable per ADR-IC-000 F1.
2. Per-event PII field annotation contract (which fields are encrypted, how marked in the envelope or schema).
3. Key rotation policy and the post-erasure projection behaviour (PII fields return null; structural fields remain in the clear).
4. Audit-trail semantics after erasure ('an event occurred at this transaction_time; payload PII is unrecoverable due to subject erasure').

Gated by DPO confirmation that crypto-shredding satisfies the operating bank's interpretation of Article 17 under PT GDPR transposition (Lei 58/2019). If vetoed, fallback is PII off-store; tombstoning is rejected.

Coordinates with ADR-PC-002 (bitemporal projection): the §6.1 candidate paths must each accept the field-level encryption envelope.

Source: §7 in 04-open-questions.md; feature-design-event-store-projections §6.2.

title: ADR-PC-002: Bitemporal projection implementation

title: ADR-000: Common evaluation criteria for all tool selections
description:
Define the shared evaluation template that every ADR (001–010) will apply. Produces a reusable criteria rubric and a short prose section that each ADR includes by reference.

## Why this exists

Each ADR will evaluate different tools against different functional requirements, but a set of cross-cutting criteria applies to all of them. Defining these once avoids drift between ADRs and forces each decision to be honest about the same hard constraints.

## Budget constraint

**Budget is effectively 0€.** This is a first-class filter, not a soft preference. It means:
- Managed cloud services (Confluent Cloud, Datadog, Temporal Cloud, AWS MSK, etc.) are disqualified unless they have a genuinely usable free tier with no credit-card-required production cliff.
- Self-hosted open-source is the default mode.
- Tools with open-core models are acceptable only if the features required by the architecture sit in the free/community tier — the ADR must explicitly verify this.
- Licensing traps (BSL, SSPLv1, ELv2, Commons Clause) must be flagged even if currently free, because they constrain future use.

## Criteria to define

1. **Cost / licensing** — total cost of self-hosting (infra, ops time) vs free tier limits; licence type and change risk.
2. **Regulatory fit** — GDPR (data residency, right to erasure), DORA (resilience testing, RTO/RPO documentation), PSD2 (audit trail, SCA). Hard pass/fail before functional comparison.
3. **Operational complexity at small scale** — how much ops burden does this add to a small team? Preference for tools that degrade gracefully when not actively tuned.
4. **Ecosystem coherence** — does it compose with the rest of the chosen stack without bespoke glue? Native OpenTelemetry, standard connectors, etc.
5. **Exit cost** — how painful is migration away in 3–5 years? Does the tool own a data format or protocol that creates lock-in?
6. **Community and longevity** — is this tool likely to still be maintained in 10 years? Red flags: single-vendor control with recent licence change, stagnant commits, small contributor base.
7. **Functional fit** — tool-specific criteria defined per ADR.

## Deliverable

A markdown section titled '## Common Evaluation Criteria' usable as a template block in each ADR, plus a summary rubric table (criteria × weight) that each ADR fills in for its candidates.

title: Q.x — Audit CI pipelines for freshness & coverage (fuzz, mutation, DB-level engine↔family independence)
description:
Periodic review of the GitHub Actions pipelines under `.github/workflows/` — are they up to date and do they cover everything they *could*? Three areas the workflows have visibly outgrown:

## 1. Fuzz coverage is pack-validate-only
`fuzz.yml` fuzzes **only** the Go `pack-validate` surfaces (`FuzzLoad` in `internal/pack`, `FuzzRun` in `internal/validate`). Every other untrusted-bytes ingress point is unfuzzed. Candidates that parse external/attacker-influenced input and arguably warrant a fuzz target:
- engine **Avro decode path** (`Babelstone.Engine.Avro` / `OutboxPublisher` inbox decode — the schema-registry writer-schema-by-id path, bd babelstone-0ho1)
- engine **command/query API** JSON envelopes (`Babelstone.Engine.Api`)
- **mcp-server** (Python) request parsing (ADR-IC-010)
- `acl` / `orchestrator` / `notification` boundary parsers
- `contracts` CUE/Avro parsing

Decide which are worth a target vs. explicitly out-of-scope, and record the rationale.

## 2. Mutation scope is 4 of ~10 .NET projects, and .NET-only
`mutation.yml` runs Stryker.NET on **EventStore, Engine, FinancialTypes (Money), FinancialMath** only. Projects that ship tests but have **no** mutation scope:
- `families/term-deposit` handler (the canonical family — arguably the most important to pin)
- `Babelstone.RateSheets`, `Babelstone.Packs`, `Babelstone.Engine.Avro`, `Babelstone.OutboxPublisher`, projection runtime (`Engine.Api`)
- **Go** `pack-validate` (no mutation tooling wired — e.g. gremlins/ooze)
- **Python** `mcp-server` (no mutation tooling — e.g. mutmut/cosmic-ray)

Decide coverage targets + score floors per `engine/docs/mutation-testing.md`, or explicitly defer with rationale.

## 3. DB-level engine↔family independence is NOT guarded
`EngineFamilyAgnosticTests` (ADR-PC-021 §P2) enforces the one-way *family → engine* arrow **at the .csproj reference level only** — it proves no spine project code-references `families/**`. There is **no** guard that the same independence holds **at the database level**:
- no family-specific tables/columns leak into the engine's event-store schema (migrations `0001`–`0011` are all engine-owned today)
- no FK from engine tables into family-owned data (or vice-versa)
- the event store stays family-agnostic (events as opaque payloads keyed by family id, not family-typed columns)
- family state lives only in family-owned projections/stores

Add a schema-level fitness function (or document why the .csproj guard is deemed sufficient).

## 4. General freshness sweep
- action pin currency (`checkout@v6`, `upload-artifact@v7`, `cache@v5`, `mise-action@v4`) — any stale/security-advisory'd?
- per-PR `changes`/paths-filter matrix in `ci.yml` — do newer areas (Engine.Api, projection runtime, rate-sheets, notification) trigger the right jobs?
- scheduled-scan cadence sanity (CodeQL 04:00, SBOM 05:00, mutation Mon 03:00, fuzz Mon 06:00)

## Deliverable
A findings note (gaps + recommendation + which to action vs. defer) and follow-up child issues under Epic Q for anything actioned. No code change required by this issue itself — it is the audit.

title: E.3 follow-up — ADR-PC-008 §S2 in-transaction rate-resolve + constitute append
description: ADR-PC-008 §S2 ('same-transaction resolution as decisive force') wants the rate-sheet resolution and the DepositConstituted append committed in ONE local transaction, so a backdated rate-sheet deploy (effective_from <= constituted_at) cannot read-skew between resolve and append. E.3 (babelstone-eyof) ships resolve->stamp->append as TWO transactions: the stamped tan_basis_points + rate_sheet_version_id are correct and frozen on the event, but the resolve+append pair is not race-atomic. This is an acknowledged, explicit divergence (allowed under ADR-PC-020 §D3 because it is recorded here, not silent).
design: Implement the in-transaction path: add tx-aware overloads IRateSheetStore.ResolveAsync(NpgsqlConnection, NpgsqlTransaction, ...) + IEventStore.AppendAsync(NpgsqlConnection, NpgsqlTransaction, ...) (the existing zero-arg-connection AppendAsync that owns its own tx — the ES_ATOMIC_APPEND_OUTBOX guarantee — stays byte-for-byte intact), plus an AggregateRuntime path; OR a generic engine 'transactional constitution' helper that owns the NpgsqlTransaction so the family decider stays Npgsql-free. Best done alongside the eventual engine host where the helper has >1 caller (pairs with the ConstitutionPipeline extraction). Touches the carefully-guarded IEventStore contract — run replay-determinism + adr-conformance before PR.

title: Central Package Management (Directory.Packages.props)
description:
Adopt NuGet Central Package Management to declare every dependency version once at the repo root, instead of duplicating Version= attributes across ~20 csproj files.

Symptom today (versions repeated across projects): xunit 2.9.3 (8×), xunit.runner.visualstudio 3.1.5 (8×), Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.6.0 (8×), Npgsql 10.0.3 (4×), FsCheck.Xunit 3.3.3 (4×), Testcontainers 4.12.0 (3×). Bumping any of these is currently an N-file edit; Dependabot PRs touch every consumer.
design:
- Add Directory.Packages.props at the REPO ROOT (not engine/). MSBuild discovers it by walking up the physical directory tree, like Directory.Build.props — a root file reaches both engine/src/** AND families/term-deposit/** (a sibling tree). An engine/-level file would miss families/, repeating the cross-tree problem that families/Directory.Build.props already works around via <Import Project="../engine/..."/>.
- Set <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>; move each version to a <PackageVersion Include=.. Version=.. /> item; strip Version= from every <PackageReference>.
- Preserve analyzer nuances: PrivateAssets="all" stays on the PackageReference; use VersionOverride= where a project genuinely needs a different pin (e.g. Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.3.0).
- Orthogonal to the existing Directory.Build.props (settings) — both compose.
- Verify: dotnet build engine/Babelstone.slnx is green; dotnet list package shows unchanged resolved versions.
acceptance_criteria: Single root Directory.Packages.props is the only place versions are declared; no csproj carries a Version= on a PackageReference (except deliberate VersionOverride); solution builds green; a version bump is a one-line edit. PR body carries the ADRs-touched/honoured section (touches engine/ build wiring) and passes adr-conformance.

title: A.8 — Event-sink seam for side-effect-free SimulationRuntime
description: Introduce an event-sink abstraction (IEventSink: durable EventStoreSink vs in-memory NullSink) so the append+outbox path (A.2) and the handler-dispatch runtime (A.6) are built sink-agnostic from day one. This enables a SimulationRuntime that runs the pure engine core for forward projection (capability #4) and counterfactual replay (#3) WITHOUT side effects — never writes an outbox row, never mints OpenBao PII material (A.5), never persists a snapshot (A.4) or projection (Epic D). Side-effect-freedom must be STRUCTURAL (the wiring isn't there), not a dry_run flag threaded through AppendAsync. → ENGINE_SIM_SINK. Emerged from the simulation-feature design review; forward projection and counterfactual replay are already committed engine capabilities (event-store §2, #3/#4).
design: AppendAsync is the single mutation point (event-store-skeleton.md §3, §4.5: 'the only place in the engine that touches the events and outbox tables') — so the sink seam goes exactly there. The footgun this story exists to prevent: implementing simulation as a dry_run boolean through AppendAsync, where one missed branch publishes a real event onto the durable bus (a correctness AND PII-on-bus compliance incident — see the outbox commit-boundary in event-store §2 and the no-PII-on-bus rule). Make it impossible by absence of wiring, mirroring how the skeleton makes 'no I/O in handlers' true by absence of a ProjectReference (§3.2). On-existing-instance simulations rehydrate read-only via A.3 then apply hypothetical future events into the NullSink. The boundary surface (MCP 'simulate' verb) and bulk dry-run gate (Q-AQ) are downstream consumers, out of scope here. May warrant a one-line amendment to event-store-skeleton.md / ADR-PC-010 pinning the simulation no-side-effect contract (run adr-conformance before that lands).
acceptance_criteria: 1) IEventSink seam exists; AggregateRuntime/AppendAsync writes through it, not directly to events+outbox. 2) A NullSink (in-memory) variant exists; a SimulationRuntime composes dispatch + fold + financial-math over it. 3) A simulation provably cannot: write an outbox row, call OpenBao/create PII envelope material, write a snapshot, or write a projection — enforced structurally (no project reference / no wiring), and covered by a test that asserts zero rows in events/outbox/snapshots after a simulate call. 4) Pack version, rate-sheet, and clock are per-invocation inputs so counterfactual inputs flow in. 5) Forward lifecycle (daily accrual / month-end / maturity) is generated by advancing the injected clock, reusing the ADR-PC-011 clock-advance pattern — not by hand-faking events.

title: ADR-PC-018: Channel routing for state-changing operations during coexistence
description:
During coexistence, a state-changing operation (e.g. open a term deposit, settle interest) lands either on the new engine (term deposits, v1) or on the legacy core (current accounts, v1-v3). Channels need a routing decision per request.

Three credible locations for the routing logic:
(a) In the channel itself (each channel knows the cutover state per product family).
(b) In a unified API gateway (the bank's gateway routes per product type to the right backend).
(c) In a unified read model (the read model exposes one query API; writes get routed via the read model's metadata).

Contract-shape ADR — should align with the operating bank's existing channel architecture, not introduce a new pattern. Pending channel-team review.

Source: Q-AI in 04-open-questions.md; feature-design-strangler-fig-coexistence.

title: ADR-PC-017: Legacy batch ingest contract

Depends on what the operating bank's legacy core can produce; unblocked by a legacy-extract audit (peer to ADR-PC-016).

design:
This issue is the consolidation point for brief edits accumulating from design-notes companion documents. The pattern in `product_concepts/` is that design-notes are written first (they're where the load-bearing detail lives), and the numbered brief is updated afterward to summarise and cross-reference them. The brief stays short by design; the design notes carry the depth.

The pattern means:
- A new design-notes document creates a new brief-edits backlog.
- The brief-edits backlog is consolidated, not handled per-document, because edits across the brief tend to interact.
- One brief-edits issue accumulates work until a worker picks it up; new design-notes consequences are appended as they ship.

When this issue is closed and a new design-notes document later ships, file a fresh brief-edits issue rather than reopening this one. Reopening accumulates context across long time horizons; fresh issues keep scope readable.

The roadmap restructure (§03 ES pack parallel track) is the highest-effort single edit and the most likely to be split out. If the worker on this issue finds it growing too large, splitting the roadmap restructure as a child issue is encouraged. The remaining edits are smaller and more interlocked.

Three persistent memories apply:
- `product-concepts-single-operator`: no commercial framing in edits.
- `product-concepts-no-calendar-effort`: project-effort framings remain forbidden in edits to the brief; falsifiable workflow + financial claims are in-scope.

title: Two-operating-modes asymmetry — design-notes companion (interfaces for v4, implementations for v1)
description:
The brief admits in `01-product-architecture.md §3` that with-a-plan (v1-v3) and irregular (v4) operating modes share the cash-flow equation but differ materially on operational profile. It warns: "the engine architecture has to be built with the irregular profile as the upper-bound design point, even if the irregular mode lands later in the roadmap. Sizing for with-a-plan only and retrofitting irregular is one of the ways 'one engine, two modes' turns into two engines under the same name." The brief states the warning but does not commit to what "size for the irregular profile from day one" concretely means.

## The asymmetry, quantified

| Property | With-a-plan (v1-v3) | Irregular (v4) | Asymmetry |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active instances | ~500k | ~1.5-3M | 3-6x |
| Events per instance per year | ~24 | ~50-200 | 2-8x |
| Annual event volume | ~12M | ~100M-600M | 10-50x |
| Peak rate | ~100k events on month-end | Sustained 100s TPS, bursts to 1000s | 100x+ at peaks |
| Per-event latency budget | Hours (accrual is batch) | Seconds (balance, fraud, overdraft) | 1000x+ |
| Event source | Engine generates internally | External transactions arrive | Opposite direction |
| Lifecycle | Bounded (constitute → mature) | Unbounded (open → close) | Different state machine |
| Failure mode | Missing accrual = recoverable | Missing transaction = customer incident | Different operational stakes |

The runtime IS the same (event handlers, projections per archie-d63). The operational profile is materially different.

## Decisions landed in brainstorm

### 1. v4 is a committed long-term goal

Not aspirational. The engine MUST be ready to absorb the irregular profile when v4 ships. The unification claim from `01-product-architecture §1` depends on this commitment being honoured.

### 2. Approach C: interfaces for v4, implementations for v1

Three credible answers (A: design for irregular from v1; B: refactor before v4; C: interfaces for v4, implementations for v1). C is the architectural commitment. Interfaces are cheap to get right and expensive to retrofit; implementations are the opposite. Reserving the v4 interfaces in v1 keeps the v4 door open without paying for v4-scale infrastructure in v1.

### 3. Six v1 architectural commitments (non-negotiable)

The six commitments that distinguish Approach C from Approach B:

1. **Event store technology with a clear scale path.** Choice deferred (see #4 below), but must support v4 throughput. NOT something that hits a wall at v3.

2. **No batch-only assumptions in core code paths.** Handler interfaces don't know about batch vs real-time. v1 may invoke them in batch; v4 invokes them inline. Same handler signature, different invocation pattern.

3. **`partition_key` on every event envelope.** Typically `instance_id`. v1 ignores it (runs unsharded). v4 uses it for routing across shards. Reserving the field in the envelope schema is free; adding it later is a breaking schema change.

4. **Projection update mechanism designed for sync OR async per projection.** Each projection has a latency budget. v1 may declare all projections async (eventually consistent within batch window); v4 marks some projections sync (current balance, available credit, overdraft check). The mechanism supports both; the choice is per-projection metadata, not engine code.

5. **Snapshot infrastructure built in v1, even if minimally exercised.** Snapshotting is the hardest part of event sourcing; getting it right takes time. Build it in v1 against modest replay needs (lifecycle boundaries, calendar boundaries); v4 turns up the frequency (every N events) without architectural change.

6. **Synthetic v4-scale load test as part of v1 acceptance.** Even though v1 won't see v4-scale traffic in production, run synthetic high-volume tests against the v1 engine (simulated TPS, simulated event volume, simulated burst patterns). Surface bottlenecks while v1 is still malleable; fix them before v4 commitment hardens.

### 4. Event store technology choice deferred to design notes

Three candidates with explicit tradeoffs:

- **Kurrent / EventStoreDB.** Purpose-built event store. Mature event sourcing patterns; native high throughput; new operational dependency for the team. Ecosystem smaller than Postgres.
- **Postgres-based.** Familiar ecosystem; scales to ~1k TPS without sharding; needs careful sharding strategy for v4. Cheaper operationally; more engineering work to scale.
- **Kafka-as-event-store (Redpanda per ADR-001).** Reuse the bank's event backbone as engine's event store. Single technology; high throughput natively; trades SQL query ergonomics for streaming-first semantics. Unusual but increasingly viable (used by some modern fintechs).

Decision deferred pending team experience and operational comfort. Design notes must capture all three with explicit pros/cons for the operating bank's specific context.

## Interactions with other in-flight design notes

- **archie-d63 (event store + projections).** This issue extends archie-d63's recommendations with operational-profile considerations. archie-d63's "battle-tested event store" recommendation refines to "Kurrent, Postgres, or Kafka — chosen for scale path to v4." The two design-notes documents reference each other.
- **archie-g1a (configuration depth).** Family schemas for irregular families (v4) declare different event types and handler patterns than with-a-plan families. The configuration model accommodates both; the design notes for archie-g1a should mention this asymmetry.
- **babelstone-119 (coexistence).** Legacy DDA's batch-file emission pattern is one async ingest source. v4 card transactions are another (real-time) ingest source. The unified read model must absorb both. Design notes should reference this.

## Open sub-questions to surface in this design notes document

- **Event store technology selection criteria.** Beyond throughput: query patterns, replay performance, schema evolution support, operational maturity. The design notes spell out the decision framework.
- **Synthetic load test specification.** What workload patterns simulate v4? What pass/fail criteria do they trigger? Who owns the test infrastructure?
- **Sharding strategy when v4 lands.** Even if v1 runs unsharded, the strategy must be designed (key choice, rebalance approach, cross-shard transactions). 
- **Real-time projection backpressure.** What happens when projection updates can't keep up with event ingestion rate? Acceptable lag bounds; alerting; recovery.
- **Cross-mode reconciliation.** A deposit maturing into a current account (with-a-plan event → irregular event). How is the cross-mode flow modelled?
- **Operational tooling asymmetry.** With-a-plan tools (manual deposit lookup, batch reports) vs irregular tools (real-time dashboards, transaction search, fraud screening). The engine's MCP server / admin APIs must accommodate both styles.

## Why this is load-bearing

The engine's identity as "one engine, two modes" lives or dies on whether the brief's promise ("size for the irregular profile from day one") is honoured concretely. The current brief states the promise; this document operationalises it. Without this document, the promise is aspirational and the failure mode is years of v1-v3 work followed by a v4 effort that finds itself rewriting the engine.

This is also the one place where the architecture has to think about v4 *now*, even though v4 is years away. Every other design decision in v1 can be made for v1's needs alone (configuration depth, coexistence, event store, projections, build-vs-buy). The two-modes asymmetry forces v4 thinking into v1 — which is exactly what the brief warned about.

title: Event store + bitemporal projections — design-notes companion
description:
A PM-mode brainstorm pass on the subledger reframed the engine's source-of-truth model. The current brief uses "subledger" as a primary concept (`00-product-vision §3`, `02-v1-scope §2.3`) but never defines its shape. This issue commits to the reframing landed in brainstorm: drop "subledger" as a primary concept; replace with "event store + bitemporal projections" with strict separation between generic engine core and family-specific event logic. This is the largest remaining architectural unknown in the brief.

## Decisions landed in brainstorm

### 1. Subledger → event store + bitemporal projections

The engine's source of truth is the **event store**, co-located with the outbox. State is *derived* by deterministic, side-effect-free event handlers. Projections (positions, accrual schedules, maturity calendar, withholding ledger) are bitemporal tables built from the event store. The CQRS read model, the GL system, and the IFRS 9 system are all *consumers* of these projections; none of them is "the subledger."

Vision document drops "subledger" as a primary concept in §3 deliverables. Open Question 3 (Time-Travel) closes — the answer is "event store with bitemporal projections."

### 2. Event taxonomy: family-specific events declared by family schemas, with cross-cutting generic events declared by the engine

The user surfaced the core tension: the engine must be generic (one engine, many families) but events must be semantically rich (audit trails, regulator-readable). Approach B from the brainstorm is the answer:

- **Family schemas declare their event types.** `TermDepositSchema` declares `DepositConstituted`, `DepositMatured`, etc. `PersonalCreditSchema` declares `CreditConstituted`, `InstallmentPaid`, etc.
- **Family schemas declare event handlers.** Pure functions `(state, event) → new_state`. The handler for `DepositConstituted` lives in the deposit family schema, not in the engine.
- **The engine code is generic.** Event-store primitives, outbox emission, handler dispatch, projection runtime, validator runtime, and a small set of cross-cutting generic events.
- **Cross-cutting events ARE generic.** `PackVersionMigrated`, `SchemaVersionMigrated`, `FundsHeld`, `AccountFrozen`, `LegacyInstanceObserved` apply to any instance regardless of family.

This is consistent with the configuration-depth answer in archie-g1a: family schemas contain everything family-specific (variants, event types, handlers, projections); the engine remains generic at every layer.

### 3. v1 event catalogue gaps

The current 8 deposit events in `02-v1-scope §2.4` are happy-path. Under event sourcing they are *insufficient* — operational events that are inevitable in production must be in the catalogue from v1 or audit trails will have gaps. Two additions:

**Cross-cutting events the engine declares (apply to all families):**
- `PackVersionMigrated` — see `feature-design-configuration-surface.md §3.6`
- `SchemaVersionMigrated` — new, per archie-g1a
- `LegacyInstanceObserved` — coexistence per babelstone-119
- `FundsHeld` — court orders, garnishments
- `AccountFrozen` — compliance holds

**Family-specific events the term-deposit schema declares (v1 additions):**
- `DepositPartiallyWithdrawn` — pack-conditional (some PT products allow partial early withdrawal)
- `DepositCorrected` — clerk-data-entry correction; needed for bitemporal correctness
- `DepositTransferredToHeirs` — succession on death of holder

### 4. GL coupling: raw business events; GL system maps

Engine emits raw business events. GL system maintains its own event-to-GL-account mapping. Cleanest architectural separation. Pushes engineering work to the GL system — coordination dependency to be surfaced explicitly in the design notes.

## Decisions deferred to design notes

- **Bitemporal implementation choice.** Three credible: PostgreSQL temporal extensions, XTDB or purpose-built temporal DB, application-level bitemporality. Each has different operational cost. To be resolved with team and operational input.
- **Replay reconciliation specifics.** Daily checksum cadence, full-rebuild frequency, event-count reconciliation per consumer. Required for "event log is source of truth" to be operationally true, not aspirational.
- **Storage and snapshot planning.** Snapshot strategy per N events / per lifecycle / per calendar boundary; replay performance targets; storage growth modelling.
- **Bitemporality regulatory requirement confirmation.** User answered "yes, mandatory" as assumed; needs compliance/audit confirmation before this is locked.

## Risk mitigations for moderate ES experience

The team has moderate event-sourcing experience (concepts understood; production-scale shipping is new). The recommendation lands with explicit risk mitigations the design notes must specify:

- Mandatory event-versioning discipline from day 1; no breaking changes to event schemas without a migration plan.
- Projection-rebuild drills as part of regular ops; not "if needed."
- Side-effect-free event handlers; side effects scheduled as separate events processed by separate handlers (the outbox is part of this discipline).
- Choose a battle-tested event store: Kurrent/EventStoreDB or Postgres-based. Do NOT build one in-house.
- Snapshots are performance optimization, not architecture; replay must work cold.

## Why this is the load-bearing architectural document

The engine's correctness, auditability, and regulatory defensibility all depend on the source-of-truth model being right. Getting this wrong is the highest-cost reversal in the brief — pack pinning depends on it, family-schema versioning depends on it, the bitemporal audit guarantee depends on it. The reframing also closes Open Question 3 and clarifies the integration architecture's relationship to the engine.

The four documents are tightly interlinked:

title: Vision + architecture revision: build-vs-buy thesis with legacy-integration ownership
description:
The current brief is silent on why the bank is building rather than buying a vendor product (Thought Machine, Mambu, Temenos, Tuum, Vault, Finxact). Under single-operator framing, this is the most consequential claim in the entire brief — and right now it's implicit. A steering committee can re-litigate the build at any point in the next 3-5 years; the brief must contain a durable, defensible answer.

## The thesis landed in brainstorm

**Load-bearing claim**: *legacy-estate integration ownership*. The bank's most valuable asset in this estate is the integration shape between core, channels, payments, CRM, GL, IFRS 9, and regulatory reporting — developed over decades and worth substantially more than any vendor engine. Buying a vendor engine forces a rebuild of that integration; building an engine fitted to the existing integration preserves the asset.

This reframes the engine: it is the new product layer that lets us use our existing integration asset with a better product model. The engine is not the headline; integration is.

**Year-5 TCO inflection (aggressive)**. Build TCO is higher than vendor licensing for the first 3-5 years and lower beyond year 5, given a stable engineering team and a stable pack-maintenance function — both of which the bank is explicitly committing to.

**Honest concessions**:
- *No single component of the engine is unique IP.* Cash-flow primitives, configuration models, and pack abstractions all exist in vendor products. The IP is the integrated fit (configuration model matching our workflow, pack maintained by our compliance team, integration fitted to our specific estate), not the components.
- *Build risk includes "we never finish."* Build-it-yourself core banking has a history of failing. Mitigations are explicit: strangler-fig adoption (legacy still runs if v1 fails), scope discipline (out-of-scope list enforced), the falsifiable agility wedge (zero engine code per variant; PM commit to production ≤ 5 working days), and a cash-flow-primitive thesis that has been mathematically validated in `financial_concepts/§9.2` independently of any implementation.

**Deferred**: the build-failure contingency is not part of the thesis. It lives in a separate risk doc not part of the brief.

## Implications across the brief

1. **`00-product-vision.md` adds a "Why build" section.** Either §1.5 between Problem and Wedge, or folded into §1. States all four pieces: claim, year-5 TCO with implied pace concession, no-single-IP concession, never-finish risk with mitigations.

2. **`01-product-architecture.md §5` reframed.** Currently §5 reads "The Integration Seam" with subsections that say "inherited from `integration_concepts/`". Under the new thesis, integration is the bank's most valuable asset and the engine's reason for existing. §5 should not subordinate integration to the engine — it should name integration as the load-bearing asset and the engine as what honours and extends it. Rewrite the framing without redefining the integration patterns themselves (those still live in `integration_concepts/`).

3. **`00-product-vision.md §4 (Out of Scope)` clarification.** Add a sentence: "Out of scope" means "we don't build the system, but we own the integration." Channels, GL, IFRS 9, payments rails, fraud, KYC are out-of-scope *products*; the *integration to them* is in-scope and is the load-bearing asset of the build.

## Hidden commitment surfaced

The year-5 TCO claim implies a delivery pace (v1-v4 collectively ship and stabilise within ~5 years). The brief deliberately stripped project-effort framings, but the financial claim implicitly commits to one. The vision must acknowledge this: "The year-5 inflection claim implies an aggregate delivery pace that the engineering team is committing to deliver against. The roadmap (`03-roadmap.md`) does not state phase windows, but the cumulative phases must complete within the inflection horizon for the financial thesis to hold."

This is the one place where the no-calendar-effort memory bends slightly: the financial claim is a falsifiable internal commitment with calendar consequences, in the same category as the workflow claims (N=5 working days, zero engine code per variant). Memory updated for both — workflow falsifiable claims and financial falsifiable claims are in-scope; project-effort framings (target windows per phase) remain out-of-scope.

title: Strangler-fig coexistence — design-notes companion
description:
The current brief treats coexistence as a thin subsection (`01-product-architecture.md §5`) and an open question (`04-open-questions.md §5`). Under the v1-done definition committed in this brainstorm — "all new term deposits on engine; in-flight mature out on legacy" — that treatment is materially too thin. Coexistence is not a steady state; it is a **multi-year period** during which two peer systems run the same product family concurrently, with seven dimensions of dual operation the brief does not currently cover.

## Scope of the design-notes document

Seven dimensions of dual operation, each needing explicit treatment:

1. **System-of-Record map.** Per product instance, name the SoR (engine vs legacy) and the rule that determines it (date-based for term deposits; product-family-based for others until v4).
2. **Unified read surface.** CQRS read model that spans both systems. Different sources have different staleness profiles.
3. **Settlement plumbing.** Engine debits/credits current accounts on legacy through the ACL (already covered by `integration_concepts/02`, but needs explicit framing for coexistence).
4. **Reconciliation.** End-of-day comparison: engine outbox vs legacy daily batch file. Alerting on mismatches. This is what Open Question 5 was asking about.
5. **Regulatory reporting under coexistence.** BdP retail-deposit statistics, FGD coverage, IRS Modelo 39 — all cross-system aggregations. Currently silent in the brief.
6. **Cutover mechanics.** Pre-cutover shadow run; cutover day; post-cutover monitoring. The first hours and days of coexistence are higher-risk than the steady state.
7. **End state.** When does coexistence end? What does legacy decommissioning look like? When the last in-flight legacy term-deposit matures or the last auto-renewal cycle completes — whichever is later.

## Decisions landed in brainstorm

1. **Legacy emission shape: daily batch file.** Legacy emits a flat file once per day. Up to 24-hour latency. The unified read model is eventually consistent within a day for legacy-sourced data; near-real-time for engine-sourced data. The read model architecture must explicitly handle this staleness asymmetry.

2. **Regulatory reporting: aggregate downstream.** The engine emits its events; legacy emits its batch file; a third system (the reporting application) combines them and produces unified returns. The engine never reads legacy data directly. This commits the brief to naming the reporting application as a real downstream system — currently it's implicit and worth surfacing.

3. **Renewal of legacy in-flight deposit = new instance on engine.** Auto-renewal at maturity creates a fresh deposit on the engine. Legacy emits `DepositMatured` (in its native format); engine emits `DepositConstituted`. The two events are linked via correlation ID and form an SoR transition. Consequence: the bulk of the legacy term-deposit book migrates to the engine within one auto-renewal cycle (3-24 months), not over the full 5-year maturity tail. Only deposits with `auto_renewal_policy = NONE` stay on legacy until full maturity.

## Open sub-questions to surface in the design notes

- **Cutover day operational risk.** On the first auto-renewal cycle after cutover, every legacy deposit that renews lands on the engine. Day-1 load could be substantial if many deposits cluster on a single renewal date. Needs a load-smoothing strategy or explicit cutover scheduling.
- **The reporting application identity.** Who owns it? Is it in-scope for this product or assumed-existing? It's not on the `00-product-vision §4` out-of-scope list, so its status is ambiguous.
- **Read-model latency contract.** Channels reading the unified portfolio see legacy data up to 24 hours stale. Is this acceptable for all channels (mobile app, branch teller, regulatory reports)? Some channels may need explicit "data freshness" indicators.
- **Reconciliation alert thresholds.** How many mismatches per day cross from "operational noise" to "something is fundamentally broken"? Needs a calibration period and SLAs.
- **Legacy batch file format/governance.** The engine consumes legacy's batch file; what's the contract? Schema? Versioning? Failure modes when legacy ships a malformed file?
- **Customer-facing channel routing during coexistence.** A customer wanting to terminate a deposit early — channel needs to know which system holds it. Routing logic must live somewhere (channel? Unified API gateway? Read model?).
- **End-of-coexistence trigger.** What's the operational signal that coexistence is over? Last legacy instance matured? Decision to force-renew remaining? Worth naming.

## Why this is the most consequential design document

The brief's value depends on v1 actually working in production. Configuration-depth is about velocity *after* v1; coexistence is about whether v1 ships at all without a split-brain incident. Every day the coexistence architecture stays underspecified is a day the bank gets closer to discovering missing operational requirements in production, where the cost of discovery is largest.

This is also the document where the integration architecture from `integration_concepts/` is most tested. The CQRS / ACL / outbox patterns are designed for event-driven peers; legacy isn't one. The design notes must spell out how the inherited integration patterns extend to a batch-file peer.

title: Configuration surface depth + falsifiable agility wedge — design-notes companion
description:
A PM-mode brainstorm pass over `product_concepts/00-product-vision.md` and `product_concepts/01-product-architecture.md` surfaced three load-bearing decisions that the current brief either dodges or leaves abstract. This issue captures them and commits to a design-notes companion document that resolves them concretely.

## What the brainstorm established

1. **v1 done = "all new term deposits constituted on the new engine".** In-flight deposits mature out on legacy. This implies a 1-5 year coexistence tail and a concrete cutover criterion: legacy DPZ constitution endpoints disabled, new endpoint on engine.

2. **Build-vs-buy rationale = architectural IP + cost/lock-in.** The bank believes its cash-flow-primitive engine is strategically better than Thought Machine / Mambu / Temenos, not just cheaper or more controllable. This is a strong claim that the vision currently hides; it should be stated directly.

3. **Multi-country within 2 years.** Pack abstraction is non-negotiable from day one. The ES pack must be a concrete artefact within 2 years, which means ES pack work overlaps v2-v3 of the roadmap, not after v4 as `03-roadmap.md` currently sequences.

4. **Configuration model = typed schemas + PM-authored YAML instances + layered authoring.**
   - **Primitives** (engine code, months cadence): cash-flow shapes, day-count conventions, withholding mechanics, etc.
   - **Family schemas** (typed schemas, ~quarterly cadence): authored by engineering + product engineering, reviewed by engineering + compliance.
   - **Variants** (YAML instances of a family schema, weekly cadence): authored by PMs/BAs, reviewed by engineer (technical correctness) + automated validator + risk (rate bands / exposure). Compliance review happens upstream at the schema/pack layer, not per-variant.

5. **Family granularity = coarse-start, fine-drift.** Start v1 with one `term-deposit` schema with optional fields covering known variant shapes. As variants accumulate distinct shapes and the schema bloats, split into focused per-shape schemas. Brief should name this evolution path explicitly.

6. **Agility wedge restored as a falsifiable claim, internal-only.** The previous editorial pass removed the '5 working days' claim because it read as a sales promise. With the staffing/workflow now defined, the agility wedge can be restated as a *testable internal commitment* rather than a sales pitch.

## Open sub-questions to resolve in the design notes

- **Exact form of the falsifiable agility claim.** Two candidates worth considering, possibly combined:
  - *Time*: "PM commit → first booked instance in production ≤ N working days end-to-end, including engineer + validator + risk review."
  - *Code*: "Zero lines of engine code per new variant; new families touch only schema + pack-binding code, not engine primitives."
  - The 'zero engine code' version is more falsifiable and more architecturally meaningful; the time version is more user-visible but depends on review cadences outside the engine's control.
- **Validator depth.** Five layers (syntactic / type-check / pack compliance / regulatory coherence / simulation). Which run synchronously at PM commit time (must be fast), and which deferred to CI?
- **Schema evolution under live variants.** Every constituted instance must pin not just to a pack version but also to a family-schema version. Architecture must state this; mechanism is the same as pack pinning in `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` §3.5 but at a different layer.
- **ES pack timing in the roadmap.** Reshape `03-roadmap.md` so v5+ (ES) doesn't start after v4; pack work overlaps v2-v3.

## Why this is a separate document, not edits to the existing brief

The existing brief (00-04) is short by design. The brainstorm output is *load-bearing detail* behind a couple of the brief's load-bearing claims (agility wedge, configurable surface, multi-country pack). Same shape as `feature-design-configuration-surface.md` — that document deepened §01-product-architecture §2 and §4 without bloating them. This new document plays the same role for the configuration-depth layer and the falsifiable agility claim.

After the design-notes document lands, follow-up issues fold its consequences into the numbered brief (vision, architecture, roadmap).
design:
This document follows the same shape and tone as `feature-design-configuration-surface.md`:
- A design-notes companion to the brief, not a numbered member of the series.
- Deepens specific load-bearing claims in the numbered brief without restating them.
- Opens new lettered open questions (Q-R, Q-S, ...) to fold into `04-open-questions.md`.
- States what changes for the brief at the end (§ Consequences for the Brief).

Three persistent memories already established for this series apply directly:
- `product-concepts-single-operator`: no commercial framing.
- `product-concepts-no-calendar-effort`: no target windows; but a *falsifiable* internal claim (time or code count) is now in-scope per user direction.
- `product-concepts-terminology`: 'the operating bank' / 'the operating organization'; not 'customer/buyer/vendor'.

The falsifiable agility claim is the one place the no-calendar-effort memory bends — it now permits a falsifiable target with a number, on the explicit basis that internal challenge is the goal, not external promise. The memory should be updated when the document lands to reflect this nuance.

(2) Inbound — messages arriving from chat platforms are HTTP POST webhooks sent to the bank's edge by the platform (WhatsApp cloud API, Slack Events API). The gateway must route these inbound webhooks to a chat adapter service that interprets natural-language or structured messages as banking commands (constitute deposit, check balance, confirm approval). The chat adapter is itself a bounded context and likely needs an ACL to translate platform-native message formats into domain commands. Decisions needed: which chat platform(s) to support; whether a single adapter handles all platforms or each platform has its own adapter; how conversational context (multi-turn saga flows) is maintained across platform messages; how human approval steps in the saga surface as interactive chat messages (approval buttons, reply-based confirmation). Deliverable: a new conceptual document in integration_concepts/ covering the chat agent channel pattern, its integration points with the existing saga/event backbone, and the trust model for inbound platform webhooks.

WhatsApp/Slack acknowledged in doc 11 only as user-side surfaces in front of the agent, not as the bank's integration concern. The async-completion subsection describes three patterns (MCP tasks capability per SEP-1686, explicit polling tool, out-of-band callback) and defers callback wire format to babelstone-087. title: ADR-011: Async saga completion notification — out-of-band callback wire format
description: The SSE stream_url pattern in ADR-006 and doc 05 assumes an actively waiting client (browser, mobile app). For sagas with workflow-approval steps that take hours or days, SSE is structurally wrong: the connection dies when the client moves on. Chat agents and async clients need a callback/webhook model instead: the initiating request includes a callback_url, and the orchestrator (or a dedicated notification service) posts the terminal outcome to that URL when the saga completes. Decisions needed: (1) callback URL registration — field on the request body vs. a separate subscription endpoint; (2) delivery guarantees — at-least-once with idempotency key on the callback payload; (3) HMAC signature on outbound webhooks so the receiver can verify authenticity; (4) retry policy for failed deliveries (transient network errors, recipient downtime); (5) which component owns delivery — orchestrator directly, or a dedicated notification service that subscribes to saga terminal events from the backbone; (6) whether the existing SSE path and the webhook path coexist (bifurcated by presence of callback_url in the request) or whether SSE is deprecated in favour of webhooks for all clients. Deliverable: decision captured in either a new ADR or as an amendment to ADR-006 and doc 00/05.
close_reason: ADR-011 written: pre-registered subscription endpoint (SSRF mitigation), at-least-once with HMAC-SHA256 + timestamp, exponential backoff 10 attempts over 12h, dedicated notification service as choreography consumer, SSE and callbacks coexist. Four implementation principles: subscription lifecycle, delivery envelope, notification service as choreography consumer, 202 response amendment.

title: Engine emits a machine-readable primitive manifest for docs-gen (replace regex-over-C#)
description:
Upgrade path for the engine-primitives reference renderer (sfnt.15). sfnt.15's
MVP parses the engine's implemented `formula_ref` set out of C# source by REGEX
(`VerifiedPack.ToConvention()` switch + the `DayCountConvention` enum). That is
brittle to reformatting: a valid re-style of the switch can make the renderer
miss cases. sfnt.15 mitigates by failing loud on a parse miss — but that is a
hard CI break, not a fix.

Trigger (deferred — pick up on need): when the regex approach starts breaking (a
`ToConvention()` reformat breaks docs-gen), or proactively if adding a second
primitive family (withholding, …) makes C#-parsing too fragile to maintain.

The fix is to stop parsing C# and instead have the ENGINE emit a
machine-readable manifest of its implemented primitives that docs-gen consumes —
single source of truth, so the resolver and the published catalogue cannot
diverge. See design.

Done = docs-gen sources `reference/engine-primitives/` from the engine-emitted
manifest (not regex); `make docs-verify` stays byte-identical and green; the
sfnt.15 regex parser is removed.

Anchors: ADR-PC-022 §P1/§P2 (generated reference, NO_DRIFT/BANNERED), ADR-PC-006,
ADR-PC-007. Run via `mise exec --`.
design:
Two options to emit the manifest:

(a) A tiny `dotnet run` tool (e.g. `tools/PrimitiveCatalog`) that prints the
    implemented {formula_ref -> convention -> description} set as JSON; docs-gen
    reads the JSON and renders the table.
(b) A `[FormulaRef("engine.day_count.actual_360")]` attribute on the resolver
    cases / convention enum members, scanned via reflection by that tool.
    Strongest form: the resolver and the published catalogue derive from the
    same attributes, so they cannot drift.

Cost: this adds a `dotnet` dependency to the docs-gen path. Today docs-gen needs
only python + mise + cue; `make docs-verify` in CI would then also need the .NET
toolchain (and a build). That cost is exactly why it is the upgrade-when-needed,
NOT the MVP — sfnt.15's regex renderer ships first; this replaces it if/when it
earns its keep.

Source: the robustness note recorded in sfnt.15's design, promoted to its own
deferred issue at maintainer request.

title: Generate an engine-primitives reference set (formula_ref catalogue) in docs-gen
description:
**Gap.** `formula_ref` (in a pack's `primitives/day-count.yaml`, and the other
`primitives/*.yaml`) is the one pack field whose validity the pack toolchain
**cannot check**. `make pack-validate` confirms the string is well-formed and
(for a variant) that the *pack* carries the day-count; it does NOT confirm the
engine implements the formula. That binding is resolved only at engine load — an
unimplemented `formula_ref` throws there (`VerifiedPack.PackDayCount.ToConvention()`),
never at validate time.

The authoritative list of implemented primitives therefore lives ONLY in engine
C# source. Unlike events (Avro), family schemas (CUE), and pack-format (pack.cue),
it is NOT rendered into the generated reference (`docs/product-management/reference/`).
So a config author has no drift-proof place to look up which `formula_ref` values
are valid — they must read the resolver switch.

**What to build.** A 7th renderer in `scripts/docs-gen/generate.py` emitting
`docs/product-management/reference/engine-primitives/`, listing the day-count
`formula_ref` values the engine actually implements, under the existing
`make docs-verify` gate (ADR-PC-022 §P2 NO_DRIFT/BANNERED). Today the resolver
implements exactly three: `engine.day_count.{actual_360, actual_365,
thirty_360_european}`. Extend to withholding `formula_ref`s (same pattern) as a
follow-on.

**Latent defect this surfaces (decide whether to file separately).**
`packs/pt.2026.1/primitives/day-count.yaml` declares
`act_act_isda -> engine.day_count.actual_actual_isda`, but `ToConvention()` has no
such case and `DayCountConvention` has no such member — the engine does NOT
implement it. It passes `make pack-validate` and would throw at engine load;
harmless TODAY only because its `permitted_for: []` blocks every variant from
reaching the resolver. The renderer would make this visible (a declared key with
no implemented row). Consider a separate Epic C / pack-correctness bug to either
implement Act/Act ISDA or drop the dead entry.

**Done =** `mise exec -- make docs-verify` passes byte-identical against a fresh
`make docs-gen`; `reference/engine-primitives/README.md` lists exactly the
`formula_ref` cases in `VerifiedPack.ToConvention()`; the page carries the
DO-NOT-EDIT banner; the root reference index (`render_root_index`) gains its row.

Source files: `engine/src/Babelstone.Packs/VerifiedPack.cs`
(`PackDayCount.ToConvention()` switch), `engine/src/Babelstone.FinancialMath/DayCount.cs`
(`DayCountConvention` enum + `<summary>` docs). Anchors: ADR-PC-022 §P1/§P2,
ADR-PC-007 (formula_ref rejected at load), ADR-PC-006.

Discovered while building the `docs/product-docs/` Diátaxis POC
(`how-to/add-a-day-count-primitive.md`): a reader asked "how do I know which
engine primitives exist?" and the honest answer was "read the C# switch."
design:
Sketch — fits generate.py's "one renderer per source kind" pattern; pure
file-read + regex, NO new toolchain dep (does not need cue/dotnet, so it runs
even when the CUE-pinned renderers can't).

Add `render_engine_primitives(slugs)` returning
`{"engine-primitives/README.md": ...}`; register in `build()`; add a row to
`render_root_index()`; update the module docstring's renderer list (currently
"Five renderers").

Parse BOTH source files and JOIN, so the page cannot silently drift:
- From VerifiedPack.cs: regex the ToConvention() switch arms
    "(engine\.[a-z0-9_.]+)"\s*=>\s*DayCountConvention\.([A-Za-z0-9]+)
  -> list of (formula_ref, enum_member), sorted by formula_ref.
- From DayCount.cs: isolate `enum DayCountConvention { ... }`, pair each member
  with the first sentence of its /// <summary> XML doc (strip tags, collapse
  whitespace) -> {member: description}.
- Emit: | `formula_ref` | Convention (member) | Description |.

Fail loud (raise RuntimeError) if: no switch arms matched (ToConvention()
reformatted -> renderer must be updated), or a switch arm maps to an enum member
that doesn't exist (engine inconsistency). This keeps the regex approach honest:
a parse miss fails the build instead of silently emitting an empty/wrong page.

Banner cites both sources: banner(f"{rel(VERIFIEDPACK_CS)} + {rel(DAYCOUNT_CS)}").
Determinism: two fixed files, rows sorted by formula_ref, no timestamps/abs
paths -> docs-verify diffs cleanly.

Brittleness note + more robust alternative: regex-over-C# is brittle to
formatting. If it proves fragile, the durable form is to have the engine emit a
machine-readable manifest of implemented primitives (e.g. a small
`dotnet run` tool that prints JSON, or a [FormulaRef("engine.day_count.actual_360")]
attribute scanned via reflection) that docs-gen consumes — single source of
truth, no parsing. That adds a dotnet dependency to the docs-gen path, so only
do it if the regex MVP starts breaking.

Mirrors sibling bd babelstone-sfnt.14 (another deferred generate.py renderer).
Run/verify via `mise exec --` per CLAUDE.md.

title: B.8b — DL 133/2009 / Banco de Portugal regulator-published TAEG anchor
description: Deferred from B.8 (archie-mi05.2): the independent external-anchor tier shipped with closed-form/spreadsheet anchors, but the regulator-published cross-check was deferred because citing a published TAEG requires the authentic figures (fabricating one defeats the tier's auditable-provenance purpose). Source the DL 133/2009 Anexo / Banco de Portugal worked example's exact CF vector + published TAEG, add it as a CorpusTier.IndependentAnchor case in FinancialMathGoldenCorpus, and assert the §6 solver reproduces the published figure. Anchors: financial_concepts §6.2.
notes:
INVESTIGATION 2026-05-27 (could not complete faithfully — keep blocked):

1. PREMISE CORRECTION: The DL 133/2009 Anexo has NO numeric worked examples. Confirmed by reading the authoritative original Directive 2008/48/EC Annex I (OJ L 133, 22.5.2008, which Portugal transposes verbatim): it contains only the present-value equation, Remarks (a)-(e), and Part II assumptions (a)-(j). The 2002-proposal example set was NOT retained in the binding text. So 'DL 133/2009 Anexo worked examples' do not exist as numbers in the law.

2. The genuine published examples live in EC guidance (2012 Guidelines SWD(2012)128; 2009 APRC study) and Banco de Portugal consumer materials — not the law. The EC PDFs returned 404/403; bportugal.pt returned 403 to WebFetch.

3. One accessible BdP example (page 'O que e a TAEG'): loan EUR 12,000 / 60 months / TAN 8% / EUR 200 initial commission -> published TAEG 10.3%. BUT a faithful reconstruction (net disbursement 11,800; 60 installments of 243.32 computed at 0.08/12; annualize monthly IRR by 12) yields TAEG = 9.1%, not 10.3%. The €200 alone moves TAE 8.3% -> 9.1%; the published 10.3% must include charges the consumer-page summary does not itemize (most likely a per-installment processing fee, which enters the TAEG). This is the 'external numbers disagree for non-bug reasons' risk noted in the issue.

NEXT STEP to unblock: obtain a FULLY ITEMIZED regulator/EC worked example — the complete CF vector with every charge (upfront + per-installment) and the published TAEG — then encode it as a CorpusTier.IndependentAnchor and assert the §6 solver reproduces it to 1-decimal precision. The kernel CAN model it (equally-spaced monthly => integer-period IRR + annualize by 12 = the directive's annual TAEG). No code was added (no faithful anchor available); B.8's closed-form independent tier already shipped and stands.
DEFERRED 2026-05-27 (owner decision): the B.8 independent tier (closed-form quadratic-IRR-vs-Newton + spreadsheet anchors on fresh inputs) gives sufficient method-independence; the regulator-published cross-check is nice-to-have hardening, not load-bearing. Reopen if/when a fully-itemized regulator worked example (complete CF vector + every charge + published TAEG) is available.

title: ADR-PC-015: IFRS 9 signal contract
description:
IFRS 9 implementation is out of scope; the signal contract between the engine and the external IFRS 9 system is in scope. Contract-shape ADR. v2-relevant (lands with personal credit) but flag now so 04-open-questions.md §2 has a tracked decision.

Three signal families:
- Staging triggers (Stage 1 → Stage 2 on significant increase in credit risk; Stage 2 → Stage 3 on default).
- Days-past-due tracking (continuous signal per exposure).
- Restructuring events (LoanRestructured with contextual data; IFRS 9 system interprets regulatory meaning).

Two shapes for the contract:
(a) One big event per staging change (Stage1To2, Stage2To3).
(b) Two signals — continuous days-past-due tracker plus discrete restructuring/forbearance events — from which the IFRS 9 system derives staging.

(b) is more compositional and reusable across IFRS 9 vendors. (a) is simpler if the bank uses a single known IFRS 9 vendor.

Unblocked by: IFRS 9 SME conversation (risk-quant or model-validation lead at the operating bank, or consultant who has integrated several IFRS 9 vendors).

Source: §2 in 04-open-questions.md.

title: Revisit ADR-011 D6: evaluate fully deprecating the saga status SSE stream for all clients
description:
ADR-011 D6 decided that SSE (the stream_url in the 202 response, doc 05 / ADR-006) coexists with webhook callbacks rather than being deprecated. The rationale was that SSE remains correct for browser/mobile clients that can hold a connection.

The question to re-examine: should the saga status SSE be deprecated for ALL clients — including browser/mobile — in favour of polling (get_process_status, Pattern 2) + callbacks (Pattern 3, ADR-011)?

Background:
- The MCP transport SSE (HTTP+SSE from spec 2024-11-05) is already deprecated and replaced by Streamable HTTP per ADR-010. That is a separate and settled matter.
- The saga status SSE is NOT Streamable HTTP's replacement target. Streamable HTTP is MCP-specific; browsers don't use MCP. If the saga status SSE were deprecated, the replacement for browser clients would be polling + callbacks, not Streamable HTTP.
- Keeping SSE means Kong must maintain the extended read_timeout and X-Accel-Buffering:no configuration (ADR-006 P4) indefinitely. It also means the 202 response carries stream_url for all clients even if most will ignore it once the webhook path matures.

Arguments for deprecating:
- One completion model (polling + callbacks) for all clients simplifies the surface considerably: one path to maintain, test, and document
- Browser/mobile clients can use polling (get_process_status) for saga tracking; the UX is slightly less real-time but adequate for sagas that take hundreds of milliseconds to complete
- The SSE path is the operationally complex one (long-lived connections, Kong read_timeout tuning, load balancer idle timeout configuration)

Arguments against deprecating:
- Browser UX for fast sagas (~700ms) regresses: instead of watching the saga complete in near-real-time, the client must poll
- Owned clients (bank's own mobile app, web frontend) should not be forced to adopt an async model that was designed for disconnected agents
- ADR-011 D6 was a deliberate decision with a sound rationale; revisiting it should require a concrete trigger

Deliverable: either affirm ADR-011 D6 (coexistence is correct) with a note on when to revisit, or produce an amendment to ADR-006, ADR-011, and docs 00/05 that removes stream_url and the SSE path.
close_reason:
Evaluated — affirm ADR-011 D6: coexistence is correct.

Rationale:
1. The 202 arrives in ~150ms; the saga finishes in ~850ms. For a browser client watching 'Processing...', SSE delivers real-time completion with zero polling latency. Replacing SSE with polling adds 0-500ms perceived latency and extra round-trips — a real regression for owned browser/mobile clients.

2. The operational concern (long-lived connections, Kong config) is already closed: ADR-006 P4 documents exactly the required Kong configuration (extended read_timeout, X-Accel-Buffering:no). Operational surface is a few lines of kong.yaml, not ongoing burden.

3. No concrete trigger exists. The issue's own text says 'revisiting should require a concrete trigger.'

Trigger conditions for future revisitation:
- If the bank's owned browser/mobile clients are redesigned to go through MCP (at which point MCP tasks + get_process_status already exist and SSE becomes genuinely redundant)
- If Kong SSE proxying produces measurable operational incidents in a production environment
- If the polling + callback path proves sufficient in a production deployment and the SSE path adds no meaningful UX benefit over polling with aggressive intervals (<200ms)

title: Cross-cutting editorial sweep across ADR series
description: Apply consistent edits across all ADRs as a single pass: (1) Audit and strike 'trivially/trivial' usages — if it is trivial, the word is unnecessary; if it is not, the word is wrong. (2) Replace softener phrases ('effectively zero', 'effectively open') with the actual constraint. (3) Audit 'may/should' inside Implementation Principles sections (ADR-003 through ADR-008); principles are normative, so prefer 'must' or declarative present tense. (4) Reduce em-dash density in opening paragraphs and dense analytical passages — three em-dashes per paragraph reads as nested asides. (5) Anchor all relative date phrases ('since 2020', 'as of 2026') to the ADR header date or a specific calendar date.
close_reason: Four targeted edits across the series: (1) ADR-004 line 134 'trivially implemented' -> 'a handful of lines' (the one remaining claim-of-trivial in the series — others matching the grep are legitimate uses of 'non-trivial' meaning 'difficult'); (2) ADR-001 line 75 'effectively zero' -> 'negligible' (the assertive form); (3) ADR-002 line 89 'effectively seamless' -> 'seamless'; (4) ADR-007 P4 'should use pseudonymous identifiers wherever possible' rewritten to 'must default to pseudonymous identifiers; raw identifiers require an explicit justification at the call site that survives code review' — strengthens the normative verb while preserving the legitimate exception path. Deliberately did NOT do: em-dash reduction (28-44 per file is mostly structural use, not nested asides — flattening it would damage the author's voice for negligible clarity gain) and broad date-anchor sweep (almost all 'as of YEAR' / 'in YEAR' references already carry a year, which is itself an anchor; the residual unanchored 'since 2020' was already fixed in P2). Most 'may/should' inside Implementation Principles are normatively-correct prohibitions ('No saga may hold...') or permissions ('Services may add...').
